title: Lore Instructions
description: Ingram's own words, 2026-09-13: 'if I want a mass edit of a document I don't have to edit everything myself I can instead write a description of a change I want to a document and you will do that work for me.' The reverse of tools/gazetteer/core/requests.py's Claude-to-Ingram queue -- this is Ingram-to-Claude, attached to a specific lore-library document. An instruction on an importance-1 document is a real fork: apply it if it is genuinely unambiguous, otherwise resolve it with status 'needs-clarification' and ask in chat rather than guessing (see design/location-rank.md's rank-1 rule and the same standing caution extended to documents in lore-library.schema.json). Consumed by tools/gazetteer/core/lore_library.py.

documentId.description: The id of the thing this instruction concerns -- usually a lore-library.json document, but since 2026-09 (issue #171) also any entity id when `source` is "approvals-desk": a `changes` bounce from the Desk reuses this same store rather than inventing a fourth one (design/approvals-desk.md §6), so this field's real meaning is 'a repo id, resolved against whichever store `entityType`/context implies' -- see `entityType`/`source` below.

text.description: Ingram's own words describing the change wanted. Never rewritten or summarised when logged -- kept verbatim so intent survives even if the edit that follows needs a second pass.

resolution.description: One line on what was actually done -- or, for 'needs-clarification', what question was asked instead of guessing.

entityType.description: Added for #171's Desk bounce: which data/ subdirectory documentId lives in (e.g. "npc", "challenge", "location") when it isn't a lore-library document, so a later reader isn't left guessing. Null for a lore-library instruction (the pre-existing, pre-#171 case) or when genuinely unknown.

raisedBy.description: Who raised this -- Ingram's own name for a Desk bounce (design/data-ownership.md's 'named rather than assumed'), null for the pre-#171 lore-library case where this was never tracked.

source.description: "approvals-desk" for a `changes` bounce (issue #171); null for the original lore-library-edit-request case this store was built for. Lets a consumer tell the two apart without guessing from documentId's shape.
